sets.title: Recognize
sets.description: Identify which element is emphasized by word order and pick between contrasting pairs
sets.descriptionRussian: Определите, какой элемент выделен порядком слов, и выберите между парами

items.prompt: Which sentence emphasizes WHO wrote the letter?
items.hint: New information (WHO) goes to the end position.
items.explanation: Письмо написал Андрей - Андрей is in final (rheme) position, answering 'who wrote it?'

items.prompt: Which is the neutral (unmarked) word order?
items.promptEnglish: Standard SVO with no special emphasis.
items.explanation: Мама варит суп - standard SVO, no element is specially emphasized.

items.prompt: In subordinate clauses, where does the verb typically go?
options: Usually at the end of the clause
items.answer: Usually at the end of the clause
items.hint: Subordinate clauses in Russian tend to have the verb closer to the end.
items.explanation: In Russian subordinate clauses, the verb often migrates toward the end: ...что Андрей написал (that Andrey wrote).

items.prompt: Existential introduction: В комнате _____ (there was a cat)
items.promptEnglish: Introducing a new entity into the scene.
items.hint: Existential sentences put the verb before the new noun.
items.explanation: В комнате сидела кошка - verb-before-noun for introducing a new entity (existential construction).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Who solved the problem? (answer emphasizes the person)
minimalPairs.explanation: Павел is in final (rheme) position, directly answering 'who?' The alternative is neutral SVO.
Глагол в начале фразы создаёт драматичное, «новостное» сообщение. Другой вариант - нейтральное высказывание.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Introducing a new character: 'In the garden there sat an old man.'
minimalPairs.explanation: Глагол перед существительным после обстоятельства места вводит новый объект (бытийное значение). Другой вариант описывает уже известного старика.

translation.hint: Verb-first puts the subject in emphatic final position.

translation.english: In the park there stood an old tree.
translation.hint: Locative + verb + new entity for existential introduction.
Adjective fronted before the demonstrative for exclamation.

errorCorrection.sentence: Пришёл Павел вчера. (meant: Pavel came YESTERDAY - emphasis on when)
errorCorrection.hint: If 'when' is the new info, it should be in final position with SVO order.
errorCorrection.explanation: Павел пришёл вчера - вчера in final position answers 'when?' Verb-initial 'Пришёл Павел' would emphasize WHO came.

errorCorrection.sentence: В парке старик сидел. (meant: existential introduction of the old man)
errorCorrection.hint: Existential construction needs verb before the new noun.
errorCorrection.explanation: В парке сидел старик - the verb must precede the new entity in an existential introduction.

errorCorrection.sentence: Ли знаешь ты это? (meant: formal question with ли)
errorCorrection.hint: The particle ли follows the verb, never precedes it.
errorCorrection.explanation: Знаешь ли ты это? - ли must follow the verb: verb + ли + subject.

errorCorrection.sentence: Что Борис купил машину. (meant: subordinate clause - 'that Boris bought a car')
errorCorrection.hint: This is a subordinate clause, not a question. The word order is fine, but it needs a main clause before it.
errorCorrection.explanation: Subordinate clauses with что need a main clause: Он сказал, что Борис купил машину. The clause itself has correct word order.
